Milio.build: Don't build armor first just because of Milio. The damage from Milio P Fired Up! and Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is magic, but Milio himself deals little damage, so choose resistance based on the enemy carry's damage type. If healing from Milio W Cozy Campfire and Milio R Breath of Life is a problem, get Grievous Wounds earlier.
Milio.combo: Once Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down and a hook angle opens, follow Nautilus Q Dredge Line → attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. Don't skip the attack, or Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root won't follow.
Milio.escape: Your chance to engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line comes right after Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is used. Milio has no mobility spell, so after closing the distance once, knock him up and lock him down with Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Milio.fight: After Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is used, close the distance with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. If the hook hits, immediately attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root, then slow him with Nautilus E Riptide. Nautilus's main magic damage is effective because Milio has relatively low magic resistance.
Milio.laning: Check whether your allied ranged carry can follow up, then cast Nautilus Q Dredge Line when Milio steps out from behind minions or an angle opens from the side. Milio's composition gets stronger as the game goes on, so prioritize early attrition and wave control.
Milio.phase: Milio's composition gets stronger as the game goes on, so in the late game Nautilus should focus on engaging and locking down key enemy targets rather than dealing damage.
Milio.teamfight: If you get an angle on Milio, target him first to cut off his healing support. Milio R Breath of Life cannot remove Nautilus R Depth Charge's knock-up, so aim your engage path to pass through other enemies too. If there is no engage angle, don't force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the front line with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide.
Milio.watch: Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is his only disengage tool, knocking back the first enemy it hits, so don't rush your engage while it is available. When Milio W Cozy Campfire is active and extends the enemy ranged carry's range, delay the frontline fight and let its duration run out. Milio R Breath of Life cleanses immobilizing effects but cannot bring airborne targets down.

Ashe.fight: Engage after Ashe W Volley is down and Ashe Q Ranger's Focus has ended. Don't walk in while enduring the slow from Ashe P Frost Shot; use Nautilus Q Dredge Line to close the gap in one move when an opening appears between minions. Once you're in, activate Nautilus W Titan's Wrath just before the enemy's damage lands and weave in auto-attacks.
Ashe.laning: Check that your allied marksman can follow up, and look for an angle when Ashe steps out from behind minions or Ashe W Volley is down. Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so don't force a cast from the front.
Ashe.build: Build armor first since Ashe's main damage is physical. Armor won't block Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow, which deals magic damage. Since Ashe relies on basic attacks and attack speed for damage, reducing her attack speed is also effective.
Ashe.combo: If Nautilus Q Dredge Line hits Ashe, follow up with an auto-attack as soon as she's pulled in to root her with Nautilus P Staggering Blow, then use Nautilus E Riptide and Nautilus W Titan's Wrath.
Ashe.escape: Ashe has no skill to create distance on her own, so engage after Ashe W Volley is down. If Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow is also down, you can approach with Nautilus Q Dredge Line without worrying about being hit by its stun. If Ashe Q Ranger's Focus is active, keep your distance until it ends.
Ashe.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals almost no damage on his own, so focus on initiating and locking down Ashe instead of hitting her directly for long.
Ashe.teamfight: When you have an angle on Ashe, aim Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path goes through the enemy team, knocking up enemies in front and opening a path for your allies to engage. After knocking Ashe up, auto-attack to root her with Nautilus P Staggering Blow, then use Nautilus Q Dredge Line when she tries to escape. If there's no angle, don't force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, and wait for the enemy's engage ability to go down.
Ashe.watch: Ashe W Volley is a slowing cone attack, so sidestep it and use the moment it's down to engage. Ashe P Frost Shot's slow is refreshed with every auto-attack, so don't stay within auto-attack range for long. Keep your distance while Ashe Q Ranger's Focus is active, and don't start a small skirmish from out of sight while Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow is available.

Alistar.teamfight: If Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, don't spend your damage on Alistar; back off and wait out its duration. If you can't retreat, new crowd control still works after he casts R, so interrupt his engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line or Nautilus R Depth Charge. When there's no angle to target an enemy carry, hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, and wait for Alistar's engage ability to go down.
Alistar.build: Build magic resistance first against Alistar Q Pulverize, Alistar W Headbutt, and Alistar E Trample damage. If you keep dying while locked down by crowd control, you can prioritize tenacity.
Alistar.combo: The basic sequence is Nautilus Q Dredge Line → auto-attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath.
Alistar.escape: Right after Alistar W Headbutt is down, use Nautilus Q Dredge Line to close the gap. If Alistar Q Pulverize is also down, use that window to reposition or engage, and stop Alistar from escaping with Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Alistar.fight: Start trading right after Alistar W Headbutt or Alistar Q Pulverize is down. If you close in with Nautilus Q Dredge Line, immediately auto-attack to root with Nautilus P Staggering Blow, then follow up with Nautilus E Riptide and Nautilus W Titan's Wrath.
Alistar.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when an opening appears between them. Don't waste it into empty space.
Alistar.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals little damage on his own, so focus on locking down the enemy carries instead of hitting Alistar for long.
Alistar.watch: Watch for Alistar to engage with Alistar W Headbutt and Alistar Q Pulverize to knock you up, then stun you with Alistar E Trample. Especially near a turret, don't give Alistar room to circle behind you.

Leona.combo: When Leona E Zenith Blade is down and an angle opens, follow Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → attack to root with Nautilus P Staggering Blow → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. If you skip the attack, the root won't follow the stun from Nautilus Q Dredge Line. If you start with Nautilus R Depth Charge, knock her up with R, then attack; save Nautilus Q Dredge Line until Leona tries to retreat.
Leona.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals almost no damage on his own, so focus on engaging and locking down the enemy's main damage dealer.
Leona.build: For your first defensive choice, consider magic resistance for the magic damage from Leona P Sunlight, Leona Q Shield of Daybreak, and Leona W Eclipse. However, choose which resistance to build based on the damage type of the enemy carry who attacks while Leona holds you in place.
Leona.escape: Leona E Zenith Blade is her only mobility tool, so right after she uses it is Nautilus's window to engage. Close the distance with Nautilus Q Dredge Line, then follow with Nautilus R Depth Charge to make it difficult for Leona to escape.
Leona.fight: Counterattack by closing the distance with Nautilus Q Dredge Line right after Leona E Zenith Blade is used. If Leona W Eclipse is active, don't fight next to her within its explosion radius; back off and wait for an opportunity. Activate Nautilus W Titan's Wrath just before the enemy's damage hits, and weave in attacks.
Leona.laning: Given Leona's high early armor, don't force a trade by leading with physical damage; counterattack after Leona E Zenith Blade is down. Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when an angle opens between them or from a bush or the side.
Leona.teamfight: Target the enemy's main damage dealer, but if there is no angle, don't force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the front line with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide. After Leona engages first and uses Leona E Zenith Blade, use Nautilus R Depth Charge as your team's engage signal. If Leona P Sunlight's mark is applied, it signals incoming follow-up damage, so don't move forward; back away.
Leona.watch: Leona E Zenith Blade pierces in a straight line and attaches to the last champion hit, so don't stand in a straight line with your allied ranged carry. Leona Q Shield of Daybreak can be activated in advance, so don't give her room to close in even if she hasn't used a spell yet. When Leona W Eclipse is active, move out of range before it explodes. If Leona R Solar Flare's indicator appears, move to the side to avoid the center stun.

Bard.watch: Bard Q Cosmic Binding stuns when it hits a wall or a second target, so don't stand with your back to a wall or in a line with an ally or minion. Bard can flank with Bard E Magical Journey, so watch the sides. Targets hit by Bard R Tempered Fate become immune to damage, so don't try to damage them during that time.
Bard.build: Get movement speed first so you can leave the warned area. Bard deals magic damage, so choose magic resistance when building resistance.
Bard.combo: When Bard E Magical Journey is down and an opening appears between minions, use Nautilus Q Dredge Line → auto-attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. Follow up with an auto-attack to root with Nautilus P Staggering Blow, and keep weaving in auto-attacks after activating Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. If you start with Nautilus R Depth Charge, use R → auto-attack → Q, saving Q until Bard tries to escape.
Bard.escape: Right after you force Bard to use Bard E Magical Journey is your window to engage. If Bard Q Cosmic Binding is also down, close in with Nautilus Q Dredge Line while avoiding the stun, then follow up with Nautilus R Depth Charge to keep Bard locked down.
Bard.fight: Close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line right after Bard E Magical Journey is down. Check the positions of walls and minions so you can avoid Bard Q Cosmic Binding, and start a fight when your allied marksman can follow up.
Bard.laning: If you see Bard W Caretaker's Shrine, walk over it to remove it.
Bard.phase: In the mid game, look for an opening when Bard E Magical Journey is down. In the late game, Nautilus deals less damage on his own, so focus on initiating and locking down the enemy's main damage dealers.
Bard.teamfight: When you have an angle on an enemy carry, use Nautilus R Depth Charge along a path that goes through the enemy team, knocking up enemies in front as well. If there's no angle, don't force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide. After the enemy's engage ability is down, signal your allies to engage with R.

Lulu.escape: Your chance to engage comes after Lulu W Whimsy is used on another ally. Lulu has no dash to create distance, so close in with Nautilus Q Dredge Line then lock her down with Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Lulu.build: Prioritize movement speed so you can get out of the area reached by Lulu's slow and area effects. Magic resistance is effective against Lulu's damage, but choose resistance based on the damage type of the ally she is protecting. Also consider tenacity against the crowd control from Lulu W Whimsy and Lulu R Wild Growth.
Lulu.combo: Once Lulu W Whimsy is down and an angle opens for a hook, use Nautilus Q Dredge Line → attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. Don't skip the attack: Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root follows Q's stun.
Lulu.fight: After Lulu W Whimsy is used on another ally, engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line from an angle that isn't blocked by minions. If the hook hits, follow with an attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root, then slow with Nautilus E Riptide. Activate Nautilus W Titan's Wrath just before the enemy's damage hits, and weave in attacks.
Lulu.laning: Stand behind minions to reduce the extra damage from Lulu P Pix, Faerie Companion. Cast Nautilus Q Dredge Line when an angle opens between minions, and pressure Lulu and her partner with steady harassment instead of forcing a single engage.
Lulu.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals almost no damage on his own, so focus on engaging and locking down the enemy's main damage dealer.
Lulu.teamfight: If Lulu R Wild Growth is available, target Lulu or someone else instead of the protected target. When Lulu uses her shield and Pix on an allied carry, that's an opportunity to go on Lulu herself. If there is no hook angle on the main damage dealer, hold the front line with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, then use Nautilus R Depth Charge as your team's engage signal after the enemy's engage spell is down.
Lulu.watch: If Lulu W Whimsy hits you, you are silenced and can't attack, so don't engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line while it is available. Lulu R Wild Growth can increase the targeted ally's health and knock up nearby enemies to prevent a kill, so don't commit all your spells to that target while it is available.

Blitzcrank.build: Build magic resistance first against the damage from Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab and Blitzcrank R Static Field. Magic resistance doesn't help against the physical damage from Blitzcrank E Power Fist. If you keep dying while locked down by crowd control, prioritize tenacity as well.
Blitzcrank.combo: The basic sequence is Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → auto-attack to root with Nautilus P Staggering Blow → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath.
Blitzcrank.escape: Engage right after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses. Blitzcrank has no skill to create distance on his own, so catch him with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and lock him down with Nautilus R Depth Charge when he tries to escape.
Blitzcrank.fight: The moment after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses is a chance to trade. Engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line when an opening appears between minions and your allied marksman can follow up. Right after it hits, auto-attack to root with Nautilus P Staggering Blow, then follow up with Nautilus E Riptide.
Blitzcrank.laning: Stand behind minions, not alongside them, to block Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab. If you don't have vision in the brush, keep away from it and use a Control Ward to secure vision.
Blitzcrank.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals less damage on his own, so focus on locking down the enemy's main damage dealers.
Blitzcrank.teamfight: Target the enemy's main damage dealers, but don't force Nautilus Q Dredge Line when there's no angle. Hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, then start the fight with Nautilus R Depth Charge after the enemy's engage ability is down. Aim Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path passes through the enemy team to knock up enemies along the way.
Blitzcrank.watch: Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab pulls the first target it hits, so keep minions in front of you to avoid it. If pulled, you can be hit by Blitzcrank E Power Fist's knock-up and then silenced by Blitzcrank R Static Field. Blitzcrank R Static Field destroys shields, so don't rely only on Nautilus W Titan's Wrath to survive.

Brand.build: Build magic resistance first. Brand's main damage is magic, and Brand P Blaze scales with your max health, so avoid building health alone. Also get movement speed to leave the warned area for Brand W Pillar of Flame.
Brand.combo: After Brand W Pillar of Flame is down, hit him with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. As soon as he's pulled in, auto-attack to root him with Nautilus P Staggering Blow, then use Nautilus E Riptide and Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. If you start with Nautilus R Depth Charge, auto-attack the airborne Brand first, then use Nautilus Q Dredge Line when he tries to escape.
Brand.escape: Brand has no mobility skill, so the moment after he uses Brand W Pillar of Flame is your chance to engage. If you're ablaze, avoid the stun from Brand Q Sear, then close in with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. Once you're in, lock Brand down with Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Brand.fight: When Brand W Pillar of Flame is down and Brand remains in range, engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. Brand has no mobility skill, so after closing in, auto-attack to root him with Nautilus P Staggering Blow, then follow up with Nautilus E Riptide. Brand has relatively low magic resistance, so Nautilus's main magic damage also lands effectively.
Brand.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when a path opens between them or you have an angle from the brush or flank. Near burning minions, step aside to avoid Brand E Conflagration spreading.
Brand.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals less damage on his own, so focus on initiating and locking down the enemy's main damage dealers, including Brand.
Brand.teamfight: Before engaging, spread out from your allies to reduce the spread of Brand E Conflagration and the bounces of Brand R Pyroclasm. Move away from your allies when you see Brand R Pyroclasm being cast. If you have an angle on Brand, aim Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path also passes through enemies in front. If there's no angle, hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide.
Brand.watch: Brand P Blaze stacks when you are hit by spells in succession, then explodes, so dodge the first spell. If you're ablaze, dodge the Brand Q Sear projectile or get behind minions to avoid the stun. Brand E Conflagration can spread near burning minions, so step aside.

Braum.build: Braum's main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. His direct damage is low, so watch more closely for the stun from Braum P Concussive Blows and the knock-up from Braum R Glacial Fissure.
Braum.combo: When Braum W Stand Behind Me is down and you have an angle that avoids Braum E Unbreakable's shield, use Nautilus Q Dredge Line → auto-attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. Auto-attack right after Q to root with Nautilus P Staggering Blow and chain your crowd control.
Braum.escape: Right after you force Braum to use Braum W Stand Behind Me is your window to engage. If Braum E Unbreakable's shield has been lowered and you've dodged Braum R Glacial Fissure, close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and catch him with Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Braum.fight: Close the gap and fight right after Braum W Stand Behind Me is down. If Braum E Unbreakable is raised toward you, don't rush to cast Nautilus Q Dredge Line; engage when the shield drops or a flank angle opens.
Braum.laning: Dodge Braum Q Winter's Bite from behind minions, and cast Nautilus Q Dredge Line when the enemy steps out from behind minions and an angle opens.
Braum.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals little damage on his own, so focus on initiating and locking down the enemy's main damage dealers.
Braum.teamfight: Target the main damage dealer Braum is protecting instead of focusing your damage on Braum. Aim Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path goes through the enemy team; you can knock up enemies along the way and open a path for your allies to engage. If there's no angle, hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, then initiate with R after the enemy's engage ability is down.
Braum.watch: Braum Q Winter's Bite slows and can start stacks of Braum P Concussive Blows, so stand behind minions. If marked, get out of range before the stacks are completed. Watch Braum R Glacial Fissure's cast animation and dodge to the side of its straight path; don't step on the lingering slow zone either.

Heimerdinger.build: Get movement speed first to leave warned attack areas. Heimerdinger's turret, rocket, and grenade damage are all magic, so build magic resistance.
Heimerdinger.combo: Follow up with Nautilus E Riptide, then activate Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and weave in auto-attacks.
Heimerdinger.escape: Heimerdinger has no skill to create distance on his own, so close in with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and, if needed, lock him down with Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Heimerdinger.fight: Don't trade head-on in front of turrets; approach Heimerdinger himself from the brush or flank. Activate Nautilus W Titan's Wrath as incoming damage lands, and weave in auto-attacks.
Heimerdinger.laning: If you force a last hit within turret range, you'll take both turret and rocket damage, so wait for an opportunity from outside. If there's no angle to engage and kill him, support an adjacent lane instead of spending time destroying turrets one by one.
Heimerdinger.phase: In the late game, Nautilus should focus on initiating and locking down the enemy's main damage dealers rather than dealing damage himself.
Heimerdinger.teamfight: When Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is available, don't bunch up in one spot in front of an objective or in a narrow passage. If an angle opens to target Heimerdinger, go around his turret setup and catch him with Nautilus R Depth Charge and Nautilus Q Dredge Line. If there's no angle, protect your allies in front with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, then initiate with Nautilus R Depth Charge after the enemy's engage ability is down.
Heimerdinger.watch: When you see the landing marker, move sideways to avoid its center; if you get hit, leave turret range. When Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is available, don't bunch up in narrow passages so you can dodge the empowered grenade.

Hwei.build: Build magic resistance first. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that only add a large amount of health. Also consider tenacity in case you take follow-up attacks after being caught by crowd control from Hwei E Subject: Torment, and movement speed to get out of ground effects.
Hwei.combo: If Nautilus Q Dredge Line hits, follow up immediately after the pull with an attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root, then use Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. If you skip the attack, you lose the root after the stun.
Hwei.escape: Hwei has no mobility spell, but Hwei E Subject: Torment can stop you from approaching while it is available. Close the distance with Nautilus Q Dredge Line right after Hwei uses it, then follow up with Nautilus R Depth Charge if needed.
Hwei.fight: Right after Hwei E Subject: Torment is used for poke or waveclear is your chance to engage. When a path opens between minions, close in with Nautilus Q Dredge Line, then follow with an attack and Nautilus E Riptide, taking advantage of Hwei's low magic resistance. If Hwei E Subject: Torment is still available, your engage can be pushed back or you can be rooted.
Hwei.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when Hwei steps out from behind them or an angle opens from the side. Missing it costs a lot of mana, so don't spend too long looking for an angle from the front or overcommit.
Hwei.phase: In the late game, focus on engaging and locking down the enemy's main damage dealer, as Nautilus's own damage falls off.
Hwei.teamfight: Check whether Hwei E Subject: Torment is available before engaging, as it can push back or root the front line. When targeting Hwei with Nautilus R Depth Charge, aim its path through the enemy team to knock up other enemies and help your team engage. If there is no angle, don't force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the front line with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide.
Hwei.watch: Hwei E Subject: Torment can make you vulnerable to follow-up attacks if it roots or displaces you. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster can deal damage based on maximum or missing health, so if the first spell hits you, move immediately to dodge the second. Also watch out for the slow from Hwei R Spiraling Despair.

Janna.build: If you need to withstand Janna's magic damage, build magic resistance rather than armor. However, Janna herself deals little damage, so there is almost no reason to prioritize buying resistance items because of her, and the information alone isn't enough to determine your first purchase.
Janna.combo: The basic sequence is Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → attack to root with Nautilus P Staggering Blow → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath.
Janna.escape: Engage during the window when Janna Q Howling Gale has missed and Janna E Eye Of The Storm has been expended. Close the distance to Janna with Nautilus Q Dredge Line, then lock her down with immobilizing crowd control. Be ready for the knockback from Janna R Monsoon.
Janna.fight: After drawing out Janna E Eye Of The Storm, engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line when an angle opens between minions. If Q hits, immediately follow with an attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root, then use Nautilus E Riptide. Nautilus's main magic damage is effective because Janna has relatively low magic resistance.
Janna.laning: Pressure Janna's protected ally to draw out Janna E Eye Of The Storm, then look for an opening to engage. Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so don't throw it predictably toward a target behind them.
Janna.phase: In the late game, focus on engaging and locking down the enemy's main damage dealer, as Nautilus's own damage falls off.
Janna.teamfight: Janna can keep pushing you away from behind her team's damage dealers, so establish vision and look for a moment when she is isolated. If you get an angle on the enemy's main damage dealer, aim Nautilus R Depth Charge through the enemy team, and consider saving crowd control to interrupt Janna R Monsoon. If there is no engage angle, don't force Q; hold the front line with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide.
Janna.watch: Janna Q Howling Gale can stop your engage with a knock-up, so avoid its path if you hear the tornado from a bush or out of vision. Janna R Monsoon pushes away nearby enemies and can reset a fight, so save Nautilus's crowd control to interrupt it. Don't dump damage quickly into a target affected by Janna E Eye Of The Storm.

Karma.build: Karma's main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. Movement speed is also useful for leaving the area left by Karma Q Inner Flame and breaking the tether from Karma W Focused Resolve.
Karma.combo: Right after Nautilus Q Dredge Line hits, auto-attack to root with Nautilus P Staggering Blow, then use Nautilus E Riptide followed by Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. If you knock Karma up first with Nautilus R Depth Charge, root her with an auto-attack, then use Nautilus Q Dredge Line as she tries to escape.
Karma.escape: When Karma W Focused Resolve is down, that's your chance to engage. If Karma uses Karma E Inspire to gain movement speed or casts a Karma R Mantra-empowered shield, close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line after the shield ends.
Karma.fight: Engage after Karma W Focused Resolve is down and the shield from Karma R Mantra-empowered Karma E Inspire has ended. When a path opens between minions, close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line, then take incoming damage with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath while weaving in auto-attacks.
Karma.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when Karma steps out from behind them. Dodge Karma's poke by moving behind minions or out of range.
Karma.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals less damage on his own, so focus on initiating and locking down the enemy's main damage dealers rather than chasing Karma relentlessly.
Karma.teamfight: Delay your engage while Karma W Focused Resolve is available or a shield from empowered Karma E Inspire is active. If you can target the enemy's main damage dealer, aim Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path also passes through enemies in front to help your allies engage. If there's no angle, hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, then initiate after the enemy comes in.
Karma.watch: If you keep getting hit by Karma Q Inner Flame, Karma P Gathering Fire lets her use Karma R Mantra more often. When an empowered Karma Q Inner Flame explodes, leave the area immediately because it will explode again. If Karma W Focused Resolve connects, get out of range to break the tether before it roots you.

Lux.build: Build magic resistance before armor to withstand Lux's damage. Also get movement speed to leave the area where Lux E Lucent Singularity is placed. Get tenacity alongside magic resistance to prepare for taking follow-up attacks while rooted by Lux Q Light Binding.
Lux.combo: After Lux Q Light Binding misses, engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and follow with an attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. Immediately after Q hits, attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root and extend the crowd control.
Lux.escape: Lux has no mobility spell, so close the distance with Nautilus Q Dredge Line in the window after dodging Lux Q Light Binding. Once you're on her, you can lock her down again with Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Lux.fight: Your chance to engage comes right after you bait out and dodge Lux Q Light Binding. Close in with Nautilus Q Dredge Line when a path opens between minions or you get an angle from the side. Activate Nautilus W Titan's Wrath just before taking damage from Lux's attacks to make use of the shield, and weave in basic attacks.
Lux.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when Lux steps out from behind them or an angle opens from a bush or the side. If you've been hit by one of Lux's spells, move out of her attack range so she can't trigger Lux P Illumination with an attack.
Lux.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals almost no damage on his own, so focus on locking down the enemy's main damage dealers, including Lux.
Lux.teamfight: Approach from different directions, spread out from your team so you don't all get caught by Lux E Lucent Singularity. If you get an angle on the enemy's main damage dealer, aim Nautilus R Depth Charge through the enemy team to help your team engage. If there is no angle, don't force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the front line with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide.
Lux.watch: If Lux Q Light Binding hits, you're likely to take follow-up spells too, so bait it out and dodge first. It passes through the first ally and can root two people, so don't stand in a straight line with an ally. If you see the red targeting line from Lux R Final Spark, move to the side.

Maokai.build: Prioritize movement speed so you can leave the areas Maokai has laid down. Magic resistance is better than armor against Maokai's damage, but choose resistance based on the enemy carry attacking while Maokai has you rooted. Consider tenacity against the roots from Maokai W Twisted Advance and Maokai R Nature's Grasp.
Maokai.combo: If Maokai W Twisted Advance is down, follow Nautilus Q Dredge Line → attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. Use the attack immediately after Nautilus Q Dredge Line to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root. If you start with Nautilus R Depth Charge, use R → attack → Q to lock the target down.
Maokai.escape: Your window to engage is right after you bait out Maokai W Twisted Advance. Close the distance with Nautilus Q Dredge Line, then follow with Nautilus R Depth Charge if available. While Maokai W Twisted Advance is ready, don't look for an engage angle near a bush.
Maokai.fight: Right after Maokai W Twisted Advance is used, close the distance with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and trade damage. While Maokai is dashing as a root mass, don't use basic attacks or targeted spells; attack after he lands.
Maokai.laning: If Maokai W Twisted Advance is ready, don't enter its range near a bush. Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it only when an angle opens.
Maokai.phase: In the late game, focus on engaging and locking down the enemy's main damage dealer, as your own damage is low.
Maokai.teamfight: Fight in open terrain so you have room to move sideways and dodge Maokai R Nature's Grasp. If there is no angle to catch the enemy's main damage dealer, don't force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the front line with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide. After the enemy's engage spell is down, use Nautilus R Depth Charge as your team's engage signal, attack the knocked-up target, then save Nautilus Q Dredge Line for when they try to retreat.
Maokai.watch: Don't enter bushes where Maokai E Sapling Toss has placed a sapling. If one follows you, lead it toward minions or monsters instead of your allies. If Maokai R Nature's Grasp comes from far away, dodge perpendicular to its direction and avoid getting hit in a narrow passage.

Morgana.build: Build magic resistance first against Morgana's main damage. If you often die while locked down by Morgana Q Dark Binding and Morgana R Soul Shackles, consider tenacity first. If long fights make healing from Morgana P Soul Siphon and Morgana W Tormented Shadow a problem, get Grievous Wounds.
Morgana.combo: After Morgana E Black Shield is down, follow Nautilus Q Dredge Line → attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan's Wrath. If you skip the attack, you lose the chain from Nautilus Q Dredge Line's stun into Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root. If you knock a target up first with Nautilus R Depth Charge, root them with an attack, then save Nautilus Q Dredge Line for when they try to retreat.
Morgana.escape: Engage while Morgana Q Dark Binding has missed and Morgana E Black Shield is down. Morgana has no spell to create distance, so close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and lock her down with Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Morgana.fight: Engage when Morgana Q Dark Binding misses and Morgana E Black Shield is down. Close the distance with Nautilus Q Dredge Line, then attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow's root and follow with Nautilus E Riptide. Activate Nautilus W Titan's Wrath just before the enemy's damage hits, and weave in attacks.
Morgana.laning: Keep minions between you and Morgana to dodge Morgana Q Dark Binding. Nautilus Q Dredge Line is also blocked by minions, so cast it when the enemy steps out from behind them or an angle opens from the side.
Morgana.phase: In the late game, focus on engaging and locking down the enemy's main damage dealer, as Nautilus's own damage falls off.
Morgana.teamfight: Don't waste crowd control on a target protected by Morgana E Black Shield. If there is no angle on the enemy's main damage dealer, hold the front line with Nautilus W Titan's Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, then use Nautilus R Depth Charge as your engage signal after the enemy's engage spell is down. Aim Nautilus R Depth Charge through the enemy team to knock up other enemies along its path.
Morgana.watch: If Morgana Q Dark Binding hits, Morgana W Tormented Shadow and follow-up attacks will follow, so move with minions between you and her. When low on health, don't walk through Morgana W Tormented Shadow. If Morgana R Soul Shackles connects, use Nautilus Q Dredge Line to get out of range before you are stunned.

Nami.build: Account for the healing from Nami W Ebb and Flow by considering Grievous Wounds first. The options listed are Executioner’s Calling and Morellonomicon. Build magic resistance rather than armor to withstand Nami’s damage.
Nami.combo: The basic sequence is Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → auto attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath. Use an auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root and keep Nami locked down after Q’s stun. If you start by knocking her up with Nautilus R Depth Charge, get an auto attack in, then use Nautilus Q Dredge Line as Nami tries to retreat.
Nami.escape: Right after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses is your window to engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. Nami has no mobility spell, so once you close the gap, keep her there with Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root and Nautilus R Depth Charge. Fight an enemy affected by Nami E Tidecaller’s Blessing only after its duration ends.
Nami.fight: Go in on Nami right after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses. Close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line, follow with an auto attack to chain Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then use Nautilus E Riptide and Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath. Nami has no mobility spell, so once you’re on her, Nautilus R Depth Charge can also lock her down.
Nami.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it through an opening between minions or from a brush or the side. Missing it costs a lot of mana, so look for an opportunity after Nami Q Aqua Prison is down.
Nami.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals less damage on his own, so focus on starting fights and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer.
Nami.teamfight: When possible, target the enemy’s main damage dealer with Nautilus R Depth Charge and angle it so its path passes through the enemy team. If you don’t have an angle, don’t force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the frontline with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide. After the enemy’s engage tools are down, use Nautilus R Depth Charge as the signal for your team to engage.
Nami.watch: Nami Q Aqua Prison falls slowly, but stuns if it hits, so sidestep when you see it coming. Sidestep Nami R Tidal Wave as soon as you see it, and save Nautilus Q Dredge Line for the Nami Q Aqua Prison that will follow. Don’t fight an enemy affected by Nami E Tidecaller’s Blessing head-on; re-engage after its duration ends.

Neeko.build: Build magic resistance first against Neeko’s main damage. If you’re likely to die after being rooted by Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and hit by Neeko R Pop Blossom, prioritize tenacity. Move speed is also useful for getting out of the area Neeko has set up.
Neeko.combo: The basic sequence is Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → auto attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath. Follow Q immediately with an auto attack to chain Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root.
Neeko.escape: Right after Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is down is your window to engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. Engage while Neeko R Pop Blossom is down as well, then follow with Nautilus R Depth Charge to lock Neeko down. Don’t miss this window while chasing her clone.
Neeko.fight: Close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line right after Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is down or while Neeko R Pop Blossom is down. If Q hits, follow with an auto attack to chain Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root and use Nautilus E Riptide. Activate Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath just before Neeko’s damage lands, and weave in auto attacks.
Neeko.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it through an opening between them or from the side when you have an angle. If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is down, use that opening to engage.
Neeko.phase: In the late game, Nautilus should focus on starting fights and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer rather than dealing damage himself.
Neeko.teamfight: Neeko can approach your team while disguised, so spread out as soon as you notice a suspicious approach to avoid getting caught together by Neeko R Pop Blossom. When Neeko goes in, stop her with a saved Nautilus R Depth Charge or Nautilus Q Dredge Line, and slow her approach with Nautilus E Riptide. If you don’t have a safe angle on the enemy’s main damage dealer, hold the frontline with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and E, then start the fight with R after the enemy’s engage tools are down.
Neeko.watch: Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows and speeds up after hitting something, so don’t stand on top of an ally. If Neeko approaches while disguised, the windup for Neeko R Pop Blossom may be hidden, so spread out as soon as a suspicious enemy gets close. Don’t chase the clone from Neeko W Shapesplitter; track the real Neeko.

Pantheon.build: Pantheon’s main damage is physical, so build armor first. Pantheon W Shield Vault deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid choices that add a lot of health alone. Basic attacks and attack speed are also key parts of his damage, so consider effects that reduce attack speed.
Pantheon.combo: When you have an opening to engage, hit Nautilus Q Dredge Line, immediately follow with an auto attack to chain Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then use Nautilus E Riptide followed by Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath. If Pantheon is using E Aegis Assault, wait for it to end or angle around to the side instead of dealing damage from the front.
Pantheon.escape: Look to engage after Pantheon W Shield Vault is down, but if Pantheon R Grand Starfall is still available, account for his ability to escape with it. Before Pantheon R Grand Starfall comes back up, close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and look for a chance to lock him down with Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Pantheon.fight: When Pantheon goes in with W Shield Vault, absorb the damage with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and slow his approach with Nautilus E Riptide. Focus your damage after Pantheon E Aegis Assault ends.
Pantheon.laning: Stand behind minions to avoid Pantheon Q Comet Spear. Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when an angle opens between them.
Pantheon.phase: Pantheon’s influence falls off in the late game, and Nautilus should focus on starting fights and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer rather than dealing damage himself.
Pantheon.teamfight: If you have an angle on the enemy’s main damage dealer, aim Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path also passes through other enemies and knocks them up. If you don’t have an angle, don’t force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the frontline with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide. After Pantheon W Shield Vault or another engage tool is down, use Nautilus R Depth Charge to start your team’s engage.
Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault stuns a targeted enemy, so be careful not to give him range. When Pantheon goes in, activate Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath just before his damage lands. When Pantheon uses E Aegis Assault, don’t deal damage from the front; wait for it to end or angle around to the side.

Pyke.build: Build health first, then armor, to withstand Pyke’s damage. Since Pyke stacks armor penetration, it’s better to secure enough health to stay above the Pyke R Death From Below threshold than to add only a little armor. Magic resistance won’t help against Pyke’s damage.
Pyke.combo: Dodge Pyke E Phantom Undertow, then chain Nautilus Q Dredge Line → auto attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath. Get an auto attack in immediately after Nautilus Q Dredge Line’s stun so Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root doesn’t break.
Pyke.escape: Right after dodging Pyke E Phantom Undertow is your chance to engage. If Pyke R Death From Below is still down, close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and lock him down with Nautilus R Depth Charge. If only Pyke E Phantom Undertow is down, check whether he still has another way to move.
Pyke.fight: Dodge Pyke E Phantom Undertow to the side, then fight where he has lost his means of engaging and escaping. If Nautilus Q Dredge Line hits, immediately follow with an auto attack to chain Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then use Nautilus E Riptide. Activate Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath just before Pyke’s attack lands, and weave in auto attacks.
Pyke.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it through an opening between them or when approaching from the side. Keep Pyke in sight as he backs away after a trade to prevent the healing from Pyke P Gift of the Drowned Ones.
Pyke.phase: In the late game, focus on starting fights and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer instead of dealing damage yourself, and watch out for Pyke R Death From Below targeting low-health allies.
Pyke.teamfight: Have low-health allies spread out to reduce the risk of Pyke R Death From Below chaining between them. If the Nautilus Q Dredge Line angle is forced, hold the frontline with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide. After Pyke E Phantom Undertow is down, use Nautilus R Depth Charge as the signal for your team to engage, and hold the target with Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root and Nautilus Q Dredge Line.
Pyke.watch: Pyke E Phantom Undertow leaves a stun along his dash path, so sidestep away from the path he traveled along. If you see a shark shadow beneath you while Pyke W Ghostwater Dive is active, move toward your allies. Watch out for Pyke R Death From Below when your health is low, and don’t stand next to an injured ally.

Rakan.build: Get a way to remove crowd control first. If you build resistance against Rakan’s damage, choose magic resistance over armor.
Rakan.combo: If Nautilus Q Dredge Line hits, follow with an auto attack immediately after the pull to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then chain Nautilus E Riptide and Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath.
Rakan.escape: Your window to engage is after dodging the knockup from Rakan W Grand Entrance or right after Rakan uses it. Approach with Nautilus Q Dredge Line, then follow with Nautilus R Depth Charge if you need to limit his chance to escape.
Rakan.fight: Trade right after the shield from Rakan P Fey Feathers is removed. If Rakan W Grand Entrance misses, close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and fight when your allied ranged damage dealer can follow up.
Rakan.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when an angle opens between them. Rakan can’t escape with Rakan E Battle Dance when he’s moving alone, away from his allies, so look for that moment.
Rakan.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals little damage on his own, so focus on locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer.
Rakan.teamfight: After dodging the landing from Rakan W Grand Entrance, use crowd control to stop him from moving in and out. Use Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path passes through the enemy team, knocking up the enemies in front and opening an engage for your team. If you don’t have an angle on the enemy’s main damage dealer, hold the frontline with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, then use Nautilus R Depth Charge after the enemy’s engage tools are down.
Rakan.watch: Rakan W Grand Entrance knocks up enemies at the landing point, so sidestep when his dash starts. Rakan R The Quickness charms enemies he touches, so don’t stand in a line; stop him with Nautilus R Depth Charge before he reaches you or put terrain between you.

Rell.build: Prioritize magic resistance. Rell P Break the Mold lowers resistance, and Rell E Full Tilt deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid choices that add a lot of health alone.
Rell.combo: After Rell Q Shattering Strike is down, chain Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath.
Rell.escape: Don’t go in just because Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down is down. Wait until Rell E Full Tilt is down too, then approach with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and lock her down with Nautilus R Depth Charge, especially before Rell E Full Tilt comes back up.
Rell.fight: Use Nautilus E Riptide in Rell’s approach path ahead of time to make it harder for her to engage. After Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down and Rell E Full Tilt are down, close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and fight when your allied ranged damage dealer can follow up.
Rell.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when an angle opens between them; don’t waste it into empty space. Look for chances to chip away at Rell’s health with magic damage from outside her engage range.
Rell.phase: In the late game, focus on starting fights and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer, since you deal little damage yourself.
Rell.teamfight: Spread out from your allies before engaging so Rell R Magnet Storm doesn’t pull several of you in together. If you have an angle on the enemy’s main damage dealer, aim Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path passes through the enemy team. If you don’t have an angle, hold the frontline with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, then start the fight with Nautilus R Depth Charge after Rell’s engage tools are down.
Rell.watch: When Rell E Full Tilt speeds up Rell and one ally, treat it as an engage signal: stop trading and move out of Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down range. Rell Q Shattering Strike breaks shields, so dodge to the side, and use Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath after Rell Q Shattering Strike is down.

Renata.build: Secure move speed first so you can get out of telegraphed areas, and get a way to remove crowd control to prepare for Renata Glasc Q Handshake and Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover. If you build resistance, choose magic resistance to counter Renata Glasc’s damage. Renata Glasc P Leverage deals damage based on maximum health, so be careful about choices that add a lot of health alone.
Renata.combo: The basic sequence is Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath. If you start with Nautilus R Depth Charge, use R → auto attack → Q to lock her down, and save Q until Renata Glasc tries to retreat.
Renata.escape: After Renata Glasc Q Handshake is down is your chance to close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. Renata Glasc has no mobility spell, so following up once you’re on her with Nautilus R Depth Charge makes it difficult for her to escape. If Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is available, keep your distance from allies as you go in.
Renata.fight: Renata Glasc has no mobility spell, so target her when Renata Glasc Q Handshake is down and an angle opens for Nautilus Q Dredge Line. If Q hits, follow with an auto attack to chain Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then use Nautilus E Riptide. Activate Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath just before the enemy’s damage lands, and weave in auto attacks.
Renata.laning: Q is blocked by minions, so cast it when Renata Glasc steps out from behind minions or an angle opens from a brush or the side. Casting Q into empty space costs a lot of mana, so don’t spend too long trying to line it up from the front.
Renata.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals almost no damage on his own, so focus on starting fights and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer.
Renata.teamfight: When Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is available, don’t engage bunched up in a line with your allies. If you can target the backline damage dealer with Nautilus R Depth Charge, aim it so its path passes through the enemy team and knocks up the enemies in front too. If you don’t have that angle, hold the frontline with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide, then use R as the engage signal after the enemy’s engage tools are down.
Renata.watch: Renata Glasc Q Handshake roots the first target it hits and can throw them to stun an ally too, so keep a minion or frontline unit between you and her before engaging. Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover makes you attack nearby allies if it hits, so keep your distance from them as you engage when R is available. If you kill an enemy affected by Renata Glasc W Bailout, pull back so an ally doesn’t die beside them.

Senna.build: Build armor first against Senna’s main damage. Senna P Absolution deals damage based on current health, so build armor along with health instead of stacking health alone.
Senna.combo: If Nautilus Q Dredge Line hits, follow with an auto attack immediately after the pull to chain Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then use Nautilus E Riptide and Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath.
Senna.escape: After Senna W Last Embrace is down, use the opportunity to engage while you can avoid its root.
Senna.fight: When Senna steps forward to collect a soul and an opening appears between minions, engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. Activate Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath just before Senna’s damage lands, and weave in auto attacks.
Senna.laning: When a soul appears, watch where Senna will move to and wait to interrupt her collection. Move out of the line between Senna and the minions in front of her, and don’t cast Nautilus Q Dredge Line into an angle blocked by minions.
Senna.phase: In the late game, Senna’s range and attack damage scale while Nautilus’s own damage falls off, so focus on starting fights and locking down Senna.
Senna.teamfight: When Senna E Curse of the Black Mist appears, back off and move somewhere with vision, or use Nautilus E Riptide on the mist area to stop an engage. If you have an angle on Senna, aim Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path passes through the enemy team and opens a route for your allies to engage. If you don’t have an angle, don’t force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the frontline with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide.
Senna.watch: Senna Q Piercing Darkness travels in a straight line through allies or minions, so move out of its path. If Senna W Last Embrace hits you, move away from your allies before the root takes hold; in lane, stand behind minions to block it. After Senna hits you once, dodge her second attack to prevent her from collecting mist.

Seraphine.build: Seraphine’s main damage is magic, so prioritize magic resistance from your first purchase. Build magic resistance over armor to withstand Seraphine P Stage Presence, Q High Note, and E Beat Drop.
Seraphine.combo: The basic combo is Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → auto attack → Nautilus E Riptide → W Titan’s Wrath. As Q’s stun wears off, extend the crowd control with an auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root. Keep weaving in auto attacks after activating W.
Seraphine.escape: The moment Seraphine E Beat Drop is down is your chance to engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. Seraphine has no mobility, so after closing the gap, chaining into Nautilus R Depth Charge makes it difficult for her to escape.
Seraphine.fight: Engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line when Seraphine E Beat Drop is down and she is separated from her ADC. If Q hits, immediately follow with an auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then chain Nautilus E Riptide and W Titan’s Wrath.
Seraphine.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when Seraphine steps out from behind them or a flank angle opens. Missing Q wastes a lot of mana, so don’t spend too long looking for an angle from the front.
Seraphine.phase: Use the moment Seraphine E Beat Drop goes down to start a fight. In the late game, Nautilus deals less damage on his own, so focus on engaging and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer.
Seraphine.teamfight: Stand spread out to either side of your allies so Seraphine R Encore can’t gain range by passing through them. When using Nautilus R Depth Charge on Seraphine, aim its path through the enemy team to knock up enemies in front of her as well. If there’s no angle to engage, don’t force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the line in front of your allies with W Titan’s Wrath and E Riptide.
Seraphine.watch: Seraphine E Beat Drop roots Nautilus if he is already slowed, and stuns him if he is immobilized. If you get hit by the slow, first move out of the straight line in front of Seraphine. In teamfights, stand spread out to either side of your allies because Seraphine R Encore gains range each time it hits an allied champion.

Sona.build: Sona’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first. Have at least one anti-heal item on your team to deal with her late-game healing.
Sona.combo: When Sona steps forward and a path opens between minions, use Nautilus Q Dredge Line → auto attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath. Follow Q’s stun immediately with an auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root.
Sona.escape: After Sona R Crescendo is down, you no longer need to hold back for its stun, so look for a chance to engage. If you lock Sona down with Nautilus Q Dredge Line or Nautilus R Depth Charge before she activates Sona E Song of Celerity, you can limit her chance to escape with movement speed.
Sona.fight: When Sona steps forward to spread her aura, engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and immobilize her. After she speeds up with Sona E Song of Celerity, don’t rely on the slow alone to chase; follow through with Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root.
Sona.laning: Minions block Nautilus Q Dredge Line, so look for an angle from the flank or a brush, and save mana if there’s no clear shot. If you keep forcing trades early, Sona will heal with Sona W Aria of Perseverance until she runs out of mana first.
Sona.phase: In the late game, Sona’s scaling and healing become stronger, so Nautilus should focus on engaging and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer rather than dealing damage.
Sona.teamfight: Don’t line up with your allies, so Sona R Crescendo can’t hit several of you at once. If there’s no angle to reach the main damage dealer, protect your allies from the front with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and E Riptide, then engage after the enemy comes in.
Sona.watch: Sona R Crescendo stuns all allies in a line, so spread out to either side of your allies when Sona steps forward. If she approaches within auto attack range as though Sona P Power Chord is ready, watch out for the empowered attack’s damage or slow.

Soraka.build: Soraka Q Starcall and E Equinox deal magic damage, so build magic resistance first. If the fight goes long and Soraka heals repeatedly, consider anti-heal next.
Soraka.combo: After Soraka E Equinox is down, use Nautilus Q Dredge Line → auto attack → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath. If you skip the auto attack, you can’t chain Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root after Q’s stun.
Soraka.escape: The moment Soraka E Equinox is used for poke or waveclear is your chance to engage. Soraka has no mobility, so close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and lock her down with Nautilus R Depth Charge.
Soraka.fight: Close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line when Soraka E Equinox is down. If Q hits, immediately follow with an auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then slow her with Nautilus E Riptide.
Soraka.laning: Check that your ADC can follow up, and cast Q when an angle opens between minions. If you dodge Soraka Q Starcall while forcing her to heal your ADC, Soraka W Astral Infusion will cost her own health.
Soraka.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals almost no damage on his own, so focus on engaging and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer.
Soraka.teamfight: Target Soraka herself instead of repeatedly hitting enemies she heals. If an angle opens to reach Soraka, aim Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path also passes through other enemies and knocks them up. If there’s no angle, don’t force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and E Riptide, then engage with R after the enemy’s engage ability is down.
Soraka.watch: Entering Soraka E Equinox’s zone silences you and can also root you. Use Nautilus Q Dredge Line before stepping into the zone, and close the gap while dodging Soraka Q Starcall, which slows and heals her.

Swain.build: Build magic resistance first to withstand the damage from Swain Q Death’s Hand, W Vision of Empire, and E Nevermove. Swain heals during extended fights with Swain P Ravenous Flock and R Demonic Ascension, so prepare anti-heal next.
Swain.combo: When Swain E Nevermove is down, chain Nautilus Q Dredge Line → auto attack → E Riptide → W Titan’s Wrath. Follow Q immediately with an auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root and keep the crowd control continuous.
Swain.escape: Just after Swain E Nevermove’s outbound-and-returning wave disappears completely is your chance to engage. Swain has no way to create distance on his own, so close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and, if needed, follow with R Depth Charge to lock him down.
Swain.fight: Engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line as soon as Swain E Nevermove is down. If it hits, immediately follow with an auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then use Nautilus E Riptide and W Titan’s Wrath while weaving in auto attacks. If Swain R Demonic Ascension is active and you have to fight for a while, back off first and re-engage after his ultimate ends.
Swain.laning: Take control early to limit Swain P Ravenous Flock’s stacking. Minions block Nautilus Q Dredge Line, so cast it when a path opens between minions or from a brush or flank.
Swain.phase: It’s best to pressure Swain early, before he stacks up. The longer the game goes, the more Swain P Ravenous Flock’s stacks put you at a disadvantage, so in the late game, use Nautilus’s crowd control to start fights and lock down the enemy’s main damage dealer.
Swain.teamfight: When Swain R Demonic Ascension is active, don’t keep fighting nearby; move out of range and re-engage after his ultimate ends. If you have an angle to engage, use Nautilus R Depth Charge along a path that passes through the enemy team to knock up enemies in its path. If there’s no angle, don’t force Q Dredge Line; hold the line in front of your allies with W Titan’s Wrath and E Riptide, then start a fight with R after the enemy’s engage ability is down.
Swain.watch: Swain E Nevermove can root you on the returning wave too, so stay out of its path until it disappears completely. Swain Q Death’s Hand hits with multiple bolts at close range, so keep your distance normally. While Swain R Demonic Ascension is active, don’t keep fighting beside him; move out of range and wait for his ultimate to end.

Taric.build: Prioritize magic resistance on your first purchase. Taric P Bravado and E Dazzle both deal magic damage, so magic resistance is more effective than armor.
Taric.combo: The basic combo is Nautilus Q Dredge Line → auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath. If you skip the auto attack, the chain from stun to root breaks.
Taric.escape: After Taric E Dazzle is down is your window to engage. Taric has no ability to create distance on his own, so catch him with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and, if needed, follow with Nautilus R Depth Charge to lock him down.
Taric.fight: Engage after dodging Taric E Dazzle or just after he uses it. Land Nautilus Q Dredge Line from an angle that isn’t blocked by minions, then follow with an auto attack immediately after being pulled in to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root. Don’t let Taric auto attack you in melee range for long; fight when your allies can follow up.
Taric.laning: Minions block Nautilus Q Dredge Line, so cast it when a gap opens between minions or you get a flank angle. Bait out Taric E Dazzle before engaging, and manage the lane so Taric can’t easily stay next to minions and auto attack.
Taric.phase: In the early game, don’t casually absorb the melee damage from Taric P Bravado. In the late game, focus on engaging and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer rather than dealing damage yourself.
Taric.teamfight: Target the enemy’s main damage dealer, but if there’s no angle, hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and E Riptide. During Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s damage immunity, don’t unload your damage; use Nautilus Q Dredge Line or Nautilus R Depth Charge to lock down enemies and run out the duration. When using Nautilus R Depth Charge on a backline damage dealer, aim its path through the enemy team to knock up enemies in front as well.
Taric.watch: Taric E Dazzle stuns after a delay, so dodge to the side when you see it coming. When Taric R Cosmic Radiance’s damage immunity activates, stop attacking and manage crowd control and positioning until it ends.

Thresh.build: Build magic resistance before armor to withstand the damage from Thresh Q Death Sentence, E Flay, and R The Box. However, Thresh’s main threat is combining his crowd control with damage from his allies, so consider tenacity as well.
Thresh.combo: If Nautilus Q Dredge Line hits, follow with an auto attack immediately after being pulled in to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then use Nautilus E Riptide and W Titan’s Wrath.
Thresh.escape: If only Thresh Q Death Sentence is down, he can escape with Thresh W Dark Passage, so don’t rush your engage. Close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line during the window when both Q and W are down, but avoid a position where Thresh E Flay can pull you toward allies.
Thresh.fight: After dodging Thresh Q Death Sentence to the side, close the gap. If Thresh W Dark Passage is also down, engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line, and use Nautilus R Depth Charge to lock him down if he tries to escape.
Thresh.laning: Look for the moment Thresh steps forward to collect a soul, but only cast Nautilus Q Dredge Line, which is blocked by minions, when an angle opens.
Thresh.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals less damage on his own, so focus on engaging and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer instead of trying to break through the armor Thresh has built from souls.
Thresh.teamfight: When targeting the enemy’s main damage dealer with Nautilus R Depth Charge, aim its path to pass through enemies in front and help your allies engage. If there’s no angle, don’t force Q Dredge Line; hold the line in front of your allies with W Titan’s Wrath and E Riptide. If Thresh W Dark Passage is thrown, quickly decide whether to use your finishing ability immediately or back off.

Velkoz.build: Get movement speed first so you can more easily leave areas where Vel’Koz has placed an area attack. Then build magic resistance against Vel’Koz Q Plasma Fission, W Void Rift, and E Tectonic Disruption, and get health to withstand the true damage from Vel’Koz P Organic Deconstruction and R Life Form Disintegration Ray.
Velkoz.combo: When Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption is down, chain Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root → Nautilus E Riptide → W Titan’s Wrath.
Velkoz.escape: Vel’Koz has no mobility, so the moment Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption misses is your chance to close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. If you get very close, Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption can knock you back, so account for the change in distance right after you engage while this ability is still available.
Velkoz.fight: After Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption misses and a path opens between minions, engage with Nautilus Q Dredge Line. Vel’Koz has no mobility, so after closing the gap, lock him down with Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root and activate Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath just before the damage lands.
Velkoz.laning: Check that your ADC can follow up, and throw your anchor when Vel’Koz steps out from behind minions. Clearing vision around the river and tri-brush creates a flank route and makes it harder for Vel’Koz to step forward and poke.
Velkoz.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals less damage on his own, so focus on locking down enemy damage dealers like Vel’Koz.
Velkoz.teamfight: When Vel’Koz R Life Form Disintegration Ray starts, interrupt it immediately with the stun from Nautilus Q Dredge Line or the knockup from R Depth Charge. If you engage first, aim Nautilus R Depth Charge along a path that passes through the enemy team to target Vel’Koz and open a path for your allies to follow. If there’s no angle, don’t force the anchor; hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and E Riptide.
Velkoz.watch: Vel’Koz Q Plasma Fission splits into two bolts at the end, so don’t dodge only to the side; move toward Vel’Koz or behind where the bolts passed. If you’re knocked up by Vel’Koz E Tectonic Disruption and hit by a chain of spells, Vel’Koz P Organic Deconstruction can trigger true damage, so if you have stacks, back off and let them expire.

Xerath.build: First, get a way to block or break free from Xerath E Shocking Orb’s stun. Then build magic resistance against Xerath’s magic damage, and get movement speed to help you leave telegraphed attack zones.
Xerath.combo: Start with Nautilus Q Dredge Line when Xerath E Shocking Orb and W Eye of Destruction are down. Immediately follow a hit with an auto attack to apply Nautilus P Staggering Blow’s root, then use Nautilus E Riptide and W Titan’s Wrath.
Xerath.escape: The window to engage is just after Xerath E Shocking Orb’s stun and W Eye of Destruction’s slow are down. Xerath has no ability to create distance on his own, so close in with Nautilus Q Dredge Line and follow with Nautilus R Depth Charge to lock him down.
Xerath.fight: Close the gap with Nautilus Q Dredge Line as soon as Xerath E Shocking Orb and W Eye of Destruction are down. When Xerath charges Q Arcanopulse, dodge to the side and look for a chance to approach while he’s slowed. Activate Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath just before the damage lands, and weave in auto attacks.
Xerath.laning: Xerath Q Arcanopulse can hit you even behind minions, so change direction when you see him charging it. If you farm while avoiding heavy damage, Xerath will eventually run low first because his spells cost a lot of mana.
Xerath.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals less damage on his own, so focus on engaging and locking down the enemy’s main damage dealer while looking for an angle to reach Xerath.
Xerath.teamfight: If you get an angle to catch Xerath, use Nautilus R Depth Charge along a path that passes through the enemy team to knock up other enemies as well. If there’s no angle, don’t force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold the line in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and E Riptide. After the enemy engages, use Nautilus R Depth Charge as the signal for your allies to go in.
Xerath.watch: Xerath Q Arcanopulse pierces minions, so dodge widely to the side when you see him charging it. Be especially wary of Xerath E Shocking Orb before engaging, since its stun makes you vulnerable to follow-up damage. When you see the cast animation for Xerath R Rite of the Arcane, dodge immediately or engage Xerath while he can’t move.

Zilean.build: Build tenacity first to prepare for being caught by the stun from two Zilean Q Time Bombs and the slow from Zilean E Time Warp. Zilean’s damage is magic, so choose magic resistance when building resistances.
Zilean.combo: Your basic engage is Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → basic attack to root with Nautilus P Staggering Blow → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath. If the target has Zilean R Chronoshift, wait until the effect ends or just after they revive before spending all your abilities.
Zilean.escape: Look for an engage after Zilean E Time Warp has been used or after you dodge the second Zilean Q Time Bomb.
Zilean.fight: Split your approach with your allies so you aren’t caught alone by Zilean E Time Warp. Once you close the distance, chain crowd control to lock Zilean down.
Zilean.laning: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is blocked by minions, so cast it when an angle opens between them or when you’re positioned to the side.
Zilean.teamfight: Line up Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path passes through the enemy team and knocks up multiple enemies, prioritizing their main damage dealers. If you don’t have that angle, don’t force Nautilus Q Dredge Line; hold your ground in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide. If an enemy carry has Zilean R Chronoshift and is hard to kill, target Zilean himself, who has no mobility and is fragile.
Zilean.watch: If two Zilean Q Time Bombs attach, they stun, so move away from allies as soon as the first bomb attaches and leave the blast radius. If you’re caught alone by Zilean E Time Warp’s slow, you’re likely to take both the bomb combo and the enemy’s attacks, so avoid engaging alone. If an enemy has Zilean R Chronoshift, don’t spend your abilities while they’re reviving; wait until the effect ends or just after they revive.

Zyra.build: Build movement speed first so you can get out of telegraphed areas. Zyra’s main damage is magic, so choose magic resistance when building resistances.
Zyra.combo: Once Zyra E Grasping Roots is down, chain Nautilus Q Dredge Line hit → basic attack to root with Nautilus P Staggering Blow → Nautilus E Riptide → Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath.
Zyra.escape: The moment after Zyra E Grasping Roots misses is your window to engage. Zyra has no mobility, so use Nautilus Q Dredge Line to get on her then follow with Nautilus R Depth Charge to keep her from escaping.
Zyra.fight: After dodging Zyra E Grasping Roots, close the distance with Nautilus Q Dredge Line from an area without plants. Zyra has no ability to create distance on her own, so once you’re on her, keep her locked down with your basic attack root and Nautilus E Riptide.
Zyra.laning: Dodge Zyra E Grasping Roots sideways, and cast Nautilus Q Dredge Line only when a path opens between minions. Step on Zyra’s seeds as you pass, but back off when an ability meant to grow them comes your way, then approach again.
Zyra.phase: In the late game, Nautilus deals less damage, so focus on locking down the enemy’s main damage dealers, including Zyra.
Zyra.teamfight: Don’t fight where Zyra has built up seeds and plants; move to another objective and fight on fresh ground. If you get an angle on a main damage dealer, use Nautilus R Depth Charge so its path passes through the enemy team. If you don’t have that angle, hold your ground in front of your allies with Nautilus W Titan’s Wrath and Nautilus E Riptide.
Zyra.watch: Getting hit by Zyra E Grasping Roots’ straight-line root can lead into plant damage and the knockup from Zyra R Stranglethorns. Move sideways at the edge of its range to dodge E. When you see R’s cast indicator, leave the area; if needed, hit terrain with Nautilus Q Dredge Line to escape.
